```text
' Start a program with no console window. Used by the MEMO scheduled task.
' usage: wscript //B //Nologo run-hidden.vbs "<exe>" [args...]
Option Explicit
Dim shell, args, cmd, i
Set shell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
Set args = WScript.Arguments
If args.Count = 0 Then WScript.Quit 1
cmd = ""
For i = 0 To args.Count - 1
  cmd = cmd & """" & args(i) & """"
  If i < args.Count - 1 Then cmd = cmd & " "
Next
' 0 = hidden window, False = do not wait
shell.Run cmd, 0, False
WScript.Quit 0
=== scripts/windows/uninstall_memo.bat
@echo off
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
title MEMO uninstaller
set "HERE=%~dp0"
for %%I in ("%HERE%..\..") do set "ROOT=%%~fI"
set "MEMOJS=%ROOT%\bin\memo.js"
set "TASKNAME=MEMO Background Processor"

echo MEMO uninstaller
echo This removes the scheduled task, the logon shortcut and the Claude Code hooks.
echo Your memory data is NOT deleted: .memory/ in each repo and %%USERPROFILE%%\.memo stay.
echo.

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%HERE%register-task.ps1" -NodeExe "node" -MemoJs "%MEMOJS%" -TaskName "%TASKNAME%" -Remove
call node "%MEMOJS%" setup claude --remove
echo.

echo To also erase the captured data, type exactly:  DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA
set /p "WIPE=otherwise press Enter to keep it: "
if /i "!WIPE!"=="DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA" (
  echo.
  echo Per repo, run this inside the repo:
  echo   node "%MEMOJS%" clear --all-repo-data --yes --confirm DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA
  echo.
  set /p "WIPEHOME=also delete %USERPROFILE%\.memo on this machine? [y/N]: "
  if /i "!WIPEHOME!"=="y" (
    rmdir /s /q "%USERPROFILE%\.memo"
    echo [ok] %USERPROFILE%\.memo removed
  )
) else (
  echo [ok] data kept
)

echo.
echo Done.
endlocal
exit /b 0

=== init
'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { repoRoot, hooksDir } = require('./git');
const { memoryDir, memoBin, sessionsDir } = require('./paths');
const repos = require('./repos');
const records = require('./store/records');
const stateReport = require('./report/state');
const { hasLegacy } = require('./migrate');
const { writeFileAtomic } = require('./util');

const MEMORY_FILES = {
  'progress.md': '# Progress\n\n(auto-written by the post-commit hook)\n'
};

const OLD_AGENTS_LINE = 'Read .memory/BRIEF.md before starting.';
const BLOCK_RE = /<!-- memo:start -->[\s\S]*?<!-- memo:end -->\n?/;
const GITIGNORE_LINE = '.memory/BRIEF.md';
const HOOK_MARK = '# memo-hook';

function createOnly(filePath, content) {
  if (fs.existsSync(filePath)) return 'skipped';
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(filePath, content, 'utf8');
  return 'created';
}

function appendLineIfAbsent(filePath, line) {
  let existing = '';
  if (fs.existsSync(filePath)) existing = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
  if (existing.split(/\r?\n/).includes(line)) return 'skipped';
  const prefix = existing && !existing.endsWith('\n') ? '\n' : '';
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
  fs.appendFileSync(filePath, prefix + line + '\n', 'utf8');
  return 'created';
}

function template(name) {
  return fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, '..', 'templates', name), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n');
}

// Write a file only when its content differs.
function writeIfChanged(filePath, content) {
  let existing = null;
  try { existing = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8'); } catch (_) { /* new file */ }
  if (existing === content) return 'skipped';
  writeFileAtomic(filePath, content);
  return existing === null ? 'created' : 'updated';
}

// AGENTS.md gets one marked block: replaced on rerun, never duplicated.
function agentsContent(existing) {
  const block = template('AGENTS.block.md');
  if (existing === null) return block;
  const text = existing.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n');
  if (BLOCK_RE.test(text)) return text.replace(BLOCK_RE, block);
  const lines = text.split('\n').filter((l) => l !== OLD_AGENTS_LINE).join('\n').replace(/\n*$/, '');
  return (lines ? lines + '\n\n' : '') + block;
}

function hookContent() {
  const template = fs.readFileSync(
    path.join(__dirname, '..', 'templates', 'post-commit'),
    'utf8'
  );
  const fwd = (p) => p.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  return template
    .replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n')
    .replace('{{NODE}}', fwd(process.execPath))
    .replace('{{MEMO}}', fwd(memoBin()));
}

function installHook(root) {
  const hookPath = path.join(hooksDir(root), 'post-commit');
  if (fs.existsSync(hookPath)) {
    const existing = fs.readFileSync(hookPath, 'utf8');
    if (existing.includes(HOOK_MARK)) return 'skipped';
    const normalized = existing.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n');
    const sep = normalized.endsWith('\n') ? '\n' : '\n\n';
    fs.writeFileSync(hookPath, normalized + sep + hookContent(), 'utf8');
    return 'created';
  }
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(hookPath), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(hookPath, hookContent(), { encoding: 'utf8', mode: 0o755 });
  return 'created';
}

function init() {
  const root = repoRoot(process.cwd());
  const report = [];
  const notes = [];

  for (const [name, content] of Object.entries(MEMORY_FILES)) {
    const status = createOnly(path.join(memoryDir(root), name), content);
    report.push([status, `.memory/${name}`]);
  }

  report.push([writeIfChanged(path.join(memoryDir(root), 'README.md'), template('memory-README.md')), '.memory/README.md']);

  const agentsPath = path.join(root, 'AGENTS.md');
  const agentsOld = fs.existsSync(agentsPath) ? fs.readFileSync(agentsPath, 'utf8') : null;
  report.push([writeIfChanged(agentsPath, agentsContent(agentsOld)), 'AGENTS.md']);

  const claudePath = path.join(root, 'CLAUDE.md');
  if (!fs.existsSync(claudePath)) {
    fs.writeFileSync(claudePath, template('CLAUDE.md'), 'utf8');
    report.push(['created', 'CLAUDE.md']);
  } else {
    report.push(['skipped', 'CLAUDE.md']);
    if (!/^@AGENTS\.md\s*$/m.test(fs.readFileSync(claudePath, 'utf8'))) {
      notes.push('hint: CLAUDE.md has no "@AGENTS.md" line — add it so Claude Code loads the memory pointer');
    }
  }

  report.push([appendLineIfAbsent(path.join(root, '.gitignore'), GITIGNORE_LINE), '.gitignore']);

  report.push([installHook(root), 'post-commit hook']);

  const sDir = sessionsDir(root);
  report.push([fs.existsSync(sDir) ? 'skipped' : 'created', '.memory/sessions/']);
  fs.mkdirSync(sDir, { recursive: true });
  records.ensureDir(root);

  const statePath = stateReport.statePath(root);
  if (fs.existsSync(statePath)) report.push(['skipped', '.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md']);
  else {
    stateReport.writeState(root);
    report.push(['created', '.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md']);
  }

  const reg = repos.register(root);
  report.push([reg.status, `repo registered (${reg.repo.id})`]);

  for (const [status, name] of report) {
    console.log(`${status}  ${name}`);
  }
  if (hasLegacy(root)) notes.push('old notes found (.memory/decisions.md, errors.md, next.md) — run `memo migrate`');
  for (const n of notes) console.log(n);
}

module.exports = init;
=== install-claude
'use strict';

// `memo setup claude` — merge MEMO capture hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json.
// Backs up first, never touches other hooks, idempotent, aborts on invalid JSON.

const fs = require('node:fs');
const { claudeSettingsPath, memoBin } = require('../paths');
const { fwd, writeFileAtomic } = require('../util');

const EVENTS = {
  SessionStart: { timeout: 10 },
  Stop: { async: true },
  PreCompact: { async: true },
  SessionEnd: { timeout: 5 }
};

function memoHandler(event, { shellForm = false } = {}) {
  const node = fwd(process.execPath);
  const bin = fwd(require('node:path').resolve(memoBin()));
  const h = shellForm
    ? { type: 'command', command: `"${node}" "${bin}" capture` }
    : { type: 'command', command: node, args: [bin, 'capture'] };
  return { ...h, ...EVENTS[event] };
}

function isMemoHandler(h) {
  if (!h || typeof h !== 'object' || h.type !== 'command') return false;
  const joined = `${h.command || ''} ${Array.isArray(h.args) ? h.args.join(' ') : ''}`;
  return /memo\.js/.test(joined) && /\bcapture\b/.test(joined);
}

function readSettings(file) {
  let raw;
  try { raw = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch (err) {
    if (err.code === 'ENOENT') return { exists: false, settings: {} };
    throw err;
  }
  if (!raw.trim()) return { exists: true, settings: {} };
  let settings;
  try { settings = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (err) {
    throw new Error(`${file} is not valid JSON (${err.message}). Nothing changed. Fix the file and rerun.`);
  }
  if (!settings || typeof settings !== 'object' || Array.isArray(settings)) {
    throw new Error(`${file} must contain a JSON object. Nothing changed.`);
  }
  return { exists: true, settings };
}

function sameHandler(a, b) {
  return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
}

// Pure: returns { settings, report: [[status, event]] }
function addHooks(settings, opts = {}) {
  const next = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(settings));
  if (!next.hooks || typeof next.hooks !== 'object' || Array.isArray(next.hooks)) next.hooks = {};
  const report = [];
  for (const event of Object.keys(EVENTS)) {
    const want = memoHandler(event, opts);
    if (!Array.isArray(next.hooks[event])) next.hooks[event] = [];
    const groups = next.hooks[event];
    let found = null;
    for (const g of groups) {
      if (!g || !Array.isArray(g.hooks)) continue;
      const i = g.hooks.findIndex(isMemoHandler);
      if (i >= 0) { found = { g, i }; break; }
    }
    if (!found) {
      groups.push({ hooks: [want] });
      report.push(['created', event]);
    } else if (sameHandler(found.g.hooks[found.i], want)) {
      report.push(['skipped', event]);
    } else {
      found.g.hooks[found.i] = want;
      report.push(['updated', event]);
    }
  }
  return { settings: next, report };
}

function removeHooks(settings) {
  const next = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(settings));
  const report = [];
  if (!next.hooks || typeof next.hooks !== 'object') return { settings: next, report };
  for (const event of Object.keys(next.hooks)) {
    const groups = next.hooks[event];
    if (!Array.isArray(groups)) continue;
    let removed = 0;
    const kept = [];
    for (const g of groups) {
      if (g && Array.isArray(g.hooks)) {
        const before = g.hooks.length;
        g.hooks = g.hooks.filter((h) => !isMemoHandler(h));
        removed += before - g.hooks.length;
        if (g.hooks.length === 0 && before > 0) continue;
      }
      kept.push(g);
    }
    if (removed > 0) {
      report.push(['removed', event]);
      if (kept.length === 0) delete next.hooks[event];
      else next.hooks[event] = kept;
    }
  }
  if (Object.keys(next.hooks).length === 0) delete next.hooks;
  return { settings: next, report };
}

function stamp() {
  return new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-');
}

function setupClaude(argv = []) {
  const dryRun = argv.includes('--dry-run');
  const remove = argv.includes('--remove');
  const shellForm = argv.includes('--shell-form');
  const file = claudeSettingsPath();
  const { exists, settings } = readSettings(file);
  const { settings: next, report } = remove ? removeHooks(settings) : addHooks(settings, { shellForm });
  const changed = JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(settings);

  for (const [status, event] of report) console.log(`${dryRun && status !== 'skipped' ? `would ${status}` : status}  ${event}`);
  if (remove && report.length === 0) console.log('nothing to remove');
  if (!changed) {
    console.log(`unchanged  ${fwd(file)}`);
    return { changed: false, report };
  }
  if (dryRun) {
    console.log(`dry run: ${fwd(file)} not written`);
    return { changed: false, report };
  }
  let backup = null;
  if (exists) {
    backup = `${file}.memo-backup-${stamp()}`;
    fs.copyFileSync(file, backup);
    console.log(`backup   ${fwd(backup)}`);
  }
  writeFileAtomic(file, JSON.stringify(next, null, 2) + '\n');
  console.log(`written  ${fwd(file)}`);
  return { changed: true, report, backup };
}

module.exports = { setupClaude, addHooks, removeHooks, isMemoHandler, memoHandler, EVENTS };
```

`cd "C:/Users/sunil/Desktop/sunil_testing_folder/whisper_flow_hackathon" && cat src/capture/capture.js src/repos.js src/util.js src/lock.js src/log.js src/git.js`

```text
'use strict';

// `memo capture` — Claude Code hook entry point and `--sweep` catch-up.
// Reads new transcript bytes since the stored offset, normalizes, redacts,
// appends to .memory/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sid>.jsonl. Never fails the caller.

const fs = require('node:fs');
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');
const { stateDir, memoHome } = require('../paths');
const { repoRoot } = require('../git');
const repos = require('../repos');
const { acquire } = require('../lock');
const { log } = require('../log');
const { readJson, writeJsonAtomic, localDate } = require('../util');
const { DEFAULT_DENY_PATHS } = require('../redact');
const { normalize } = require('./claude');
const sessions = require('../store/sessions');

const STDIN_MAX = 1024 * 1024;
const STDIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000;
const MAX_TOOL_IDS = 500;

function readStdin() {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    if (process.stdin.isTTY) return resolve('');
    const chunks = [];
    let size = 0;
    let done = false;
    const finish = () => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      process.stdin.pause();
      resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'));
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(finish, STDIN_TIMEOUT_MS);
    process.stdin.on('data', (c) => {
      size += c.length;
      if (size > STDIN_MAX) return finish();
      chunks.push(c);
    });
    process.stdin.on('end', finish);
    process.stdin.on('error', finish);
  });
}

function loadDenyPaths() {
  try {
    const cfg = readJson(path.join(memoHome(), 'config.json'), null);
    if (cfg && Array.isArray(cfg.denyPaths)) return cfg.denyPaths;
  } catch (_) { /* bad config → defaults */ }
  return DEFAULT_DENY_PATHS;
}

function cursorsPath(repoId) {
  return path.join(stateDir(repoId), 'cursors.json');
}

function trimTools(tools) {
  const keys = Object.keys(tools);
  if (keys.length <= MAX_TOOL_IDS) return tools;
  const out = {};
  for (const k of keys.slice(-MAX_TOOL_IDS)) out[k] = tools[k];
  return out;
}

function readRange(file, start, end) {
  const len = end - start;
  const buf = Buffer.alloc(len);
  const fd = fs.openSync(file, 'r');
  try {
    let read = 0;
    while (read < len) {
      const n = fs.readSync(fd, buf, read, len - read, start + read);
      if (n === 0) break;
      read += n;
    }
    return buf.subarray(0, read);
  } finally {
    fs.closeSync(fd);
  }
}

/**
 * Capture one session of one registered repo.
 * @returns {{status: string, newEvents: number}}
 */
function captureSession({ repo, sid, transcriptPath, event = 'sweep', source, lockWaitMs = 1500 }) {
  const root = repo.root;
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const sid8 = String(sid).slice(0, 8);
  if (!sessions.validSid(sid)) {
    log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, status: 'invalid_sid' });
    return { status: 'invalid_sid', newEvents: 0 };
  }
  const lock = acquire(path.join(stateDir(repo.id), 'capture.lock'), { staleMs: 60000, waitMs: lockWaitMs });
  if (!lock) {
    log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status: 'busy' });
    return { status: 'busy', newEvents: 0 };
  }
  if (lock.recovered) log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status: 'stale_lock_recovered' });
  try {
    const cPath = cursorsPath(repo.id);
    const cursors = readJson(cPath, {});
    let cur = cursors[sid];
    const tPath = transcriptPath || (cur && cur.transcriptPath);
    const index = sessions.loadIndex(root);
    const before = JSON.stringify(index);
    let entry = index.find((e) => e.sid === sid);

    // Deleted by `memo clear` — never import it again from the Claude transcript (P5).
    if (entry && entry.deletedAt) {
      const cursors = readJson(cursorsPath(repo.id), {});
      if (cursors[sid]) {
        delete cursors[sid];
        writeJsonAtomic(cursorsPath(repo.id), cursors);
      }
      log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status: 'tombstoned' });
      return { status: 'tombstoned', newEvents: 0 };
    }

    const setStatus = () => {
      if (!entry) return;
      if (event === 'SessionEnd') entry.status = 'ended';
      else if (event === 'SessionStart' || (entry.status === 'transcript_missing' && event !== 'sweep')) entry.status = 'active';
    };
    const saveIndexIfChanged = () => {
      if (JSON.stringify(index) !== before) sessions.saveIndex(root, index);
    };

    let stat = null;
    if (tPath) {
      try { stat = fs.statSync(tPath); } catch (_) { stat = null; }
    }
    if (!stat) {
      // SessionStart may fire before the transcript file exists: remember the path, no gap.
      if (tPath && (!cur || cur.transcriptPath !== tPath)) {
        cursors[sid] = { ...(cur || { offset: 0, lineNo: 0, tools: {} }), transcriptPath: tPath };
        writeJsonAtomic(cPath, cursors);
      }
      let status = tPath ? 'transcript_missing' : 'no_transcript';
      if (event === 'SessionStart' && !entry) status = 'waiting_for_transcript';
      else if (entry && event !== 'SessionEnd') entry.status = 'transcript_missing';
      setStatus();
      saveIndexIfChanged();
      log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status, ms: Date.now() - t0 });
      return { status, newEvents: 0 };
    }

    if (!cur) cur = { transcriptPath: tPath, offset: 0, lineNo: 0, tools: {} };
    cur.transcriptPath = tPath;
    cur.tools = cur.tools || {};
    let status = 'ok';
    if (stat.size < cur.offset) {
      log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status: 'transcript_rewritten', oldOffset: cur.offset, size: stat.size });
      cur.offset = 0;
      cur.lineNo = 0;
      status = 'transcript_rewritten';
    }

    const envelopes = [];
    let badLines = 0;
    let consumed = 0;
    if (stat.size > cur.offset) {
      const buf = readRange(tPath, cur.offset, stat.size);
      const lastNl = buf.lastIndexOf(0x0a);
      if (lastNl >= 0) {
        consumed = lastNl + 1;
        const text = buf.subarray(0, consumed).toString('utf8');
        const ctx = { sid, root, cwd: root, home: os.homedir(), tools: cur.tools, denyPaths: loadDenyPaths() };
        for (const rawLine of text.slice(0, -1).split('\n')) {
          cur.lineNo++;
          const raw = rawLine.replace(/\r$/, '');
          if (!raw.trim()) continue;
          let obj;
          try { obj = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (_) {
            badLines++;
            log('capture', { event, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status: 'bad_line', line: cur.lineNo });
            continue;
          }
          ctx.lineNo = cur.lineNo;
          ctx.raw = raw;
          for (const env of normalize(obj, ctx)) envelopes.push(env);
        }
      }
      // bytes after the last "\n" are an incomplete line: left for the next run
    }

    let added = [];
    if (envelopes.length > 0) {
      const date = entry ? entry.date : localDate(envelopes[0].ts);
      const file = sessions.sessionFile(root, date, sid);
      const existing = sessions.readExisting(file);
      let seq = existing.lastSeq;
      for (const env of envelopes) {
        if (existing.ids.has(env.id)) continue;
        existing.ids.add(env.id);
        seq++;
        const { v, id, sid: s, ts, agent, type, ...rest } = env;
        added.push({ v, id, sid: s, seq, ts, agent, type, ...rest });
      }
      sessions.appendEvents(file, added);
      if (added.length > 0) {
        if (!entry) {
          entry = { sid, agent: 'claude-code', date, start: added[0].ts, end: added[0].ts, events: 0, processedThrough: 0, summary: '', status: 'active' };
          index.push(entry);
        }
        entry.events = seq;
        entry.end = added[added.length - 1].ts;
      }
    }

    cur.offset += consumed;
    cur.fileSize = stat.size;
    if (added.length > 0) cur.lastEventId = added[added.length - 1].id;
    cur.tools = trimTools(cur.tools);
    cursors[sid] = cur;
    writeJsonAtomic(cPath, cursors);

    setStatus();
    saveIndexIfChanged();
    log('capture', { event, source, repo: repo.id, sid: sid8, status, newEvents: added.length, badLines, ms: Date.now() - t0 });
    return { status, newEvents: added.length };
  } finally {
    lock.release();
  }
}

// Catch up every known session of one repo. Never throws.
function sweepRepo(repo) {
  const results = [];
  let cursors = {};
  try { cursors = readJson(cursorsPath(repo.id), {}); } catch (err) {
    log('capture', { event: 'sweep', repo: repo.id, status: 'bad_cursors', error: err.message });
    return results;
  }
  for (const sid of Object.keys(cursors)) {
    try {
      results.push({ repo: repo.id, sid, ...captureSession({ repo, sid, event: 'sweep', lockWaitMs: 5000 }) });
    } catch (err) {
      log('capture', { event: 'sweep', repo: repo.id, sid: sid.slice(0, 8), status: 'error', error: err.message });
      results.push({ repo: repo.id, sid, status: 'error', newEvents: 0 });
    }
  }
  return results;
}

function sweep() {
  const results = [];
  for (const repo of repos.load()) {
    if (!repo.enabled) continue;
    for (const r of sweepRepo(repo)) results.push(r);
  }
  return results;
}

async function hookEntry() {
  const raw = await readStdin();
  let data;
  try { data = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (_) {
    log('capture', { event: 'unknown', status: 'bad_stdin', bytes: raw.length });
    return;
  }
  const event = String(data.hook_event_name || 'unknown');
  const cwd = data.cwd || process.cwd();
  let root;
  try { root = repoRoot(cwd); } catch (_) {
    log('capture', { event, status: 'skip_not_git' });
    return;
  }
  const repo = repos.find(root);
  if (!repo || repo.enabled === false) {
    log('capture', { event, status: 'skip_unregistered' });
    return;
  }
  captureSession({
    repo,
    sid: data.session_id,
    transcriptPath: data.transcript_path,
    event,
    source: data.source || data.reason,
    lockWaitMs: event === 'SessionEnd' ? 800 : 1500
  });
  if (event === 'SessionStart') printContext(root);
}

// SessionStart stdout is added to Claude's context. fs.writeSync: the caller exits right after.
function printContext(root) {
  try {
    const text = require('../context').buildContext(root);
    if (text) fs.writeSync(1, text);
  } catch (err) {
    log('capture', { event: 'SessionStart', status: 'context_error', error: err.message });
  }
}

// CLI: always resolves, never throws.
async function command(argv = []) {
  try {
    if (argv.includes('--sweep')) {
      const results = sweep();
      const total = results.reduce((n, r) => n + (r.newEvents || 0), 0);
      if (process.stdout.isTTY || argv.includes('--verbose')) {
        console.log(`swept ${results.length} session(s), ${total} new event(s)`);
      }
      return;
    }
    await hookEntry();
  } catch (err) {
    log('capture', { status: 'error', error: err && err.message ? err.message : String(err) });
  }
}

function sha1(text) {

function writeFileAtomic(filePath, content) {

  fs.writeFileSync(tmp, content, 'utf8');

  }

}

function pad(n, w = 2) {

// ISO 8601 in local time with offset, e.g. 2026-10-22T14:03:11.120+05:30
function isoLocal(input) {

  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime())) return isoLocal(new Date());
  const off = -d.getTimezoneOffset();
  const sign = off >= 0 ? '+' : '-';
  const abs = Math.abs(off);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}` +
    `T${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}:${pad(d.getSeconds())}.${pad(d.getMilliseconds(), 3)}` +
    `${sign}${pad(Math.floor(abs / 60))}:${pad(abs % 60)}`;
}

// Local calendar date YYYY-MM-DD
function localDate(input) {

}

function sleepMs(ms) {

}

module.exports = { sha1, fwd, writeFileAtomic, writeJsonAtomic, readJson, isoLocal, localDate, sleepMs };

const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');

// Exclusive lock file. Returns { release, recovered } or null when busy.
// A lock older than staleMs is taken over (recovered: true).
function acquire(lockPath, { staleMs = 60000, waitMs = 0 } = {}) {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(lockPath), { recursive: true });
  const deadline = Date.now() + waitMs;
  let recovered = false;
  for (;;) {
    try {
      const fd = fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx');
      fs.writeSync(fd, JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid, startedAt: new Date().toISOString() }));
      fs.closeSync(fd);
      let released = false;
      return {
        recovered,
        release() {
          if (released) return;
          released = true;
          try { fs.unlinkSync(lockPath); } catch (_) { /* already gone */ }
        }
      };
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err;
    }
    let age = 0;
    try { age = Date.now() - fs.statSync(lockPath).mtimeMs; } catch (_) { continue; }
    if (age > staleMs) {
      try { fs.unlinkSync(lockPath); recovered = true; } catch (_) { /* raced */ }
      continue;
    }
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) return null;
    sleepMs(50);
  }
}

module.exports = { acquire };

const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');
const { logsDir } = require('./paths');
const { isoLocal } = require('./util');

const MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;

// Append one JSON line to ~/.memo/logs/<name>.jsonl. Never throws.
function log(name, fields) {
  try {
    const dir = logsDir();
    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const file = path.join(dir, `${name}.jsonl`);
    try {
      if (fs.statSync(file).size > MAX_BYTES) fs.renameSync(file, `${file}.1`);
    } catch (_) { /* missing file is fine */ }
    fs.appendFileSync(file, JSON.stringify({ ts: isoLocal(), ...fields }) + '\n', 'utf8');
  } catch (_) {
    // Logging must never break a hook or a commit.
  }
}

module.exports = { log, MAX_BYTES };
'use strict';

const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
const path = require('path');

function run(args, cwd) {
  return execFileSync('git', args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] }).trim();
}

function repoRoot(cwd) {
  try {
    return run(['rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'], cwd);
  } catch (err) {
    throw new Error('Not inside a git repo');
  }
}

function hooksDir(root) {
  const p = run(['rev-parse', '--git-path', 'hooks'], root);
  return path.resolve(root, p);
}

function lastCommit(root) {
  const output = run(['log', '-1', '--format=%h%x1f%s'], root);
  const separator = output.indexOf('\x1f');
  if (separator === -1) throw new Error('Unable to read last commit');
  return { hash: output.slice(0, separator), subject: output.slice(separator + 1) };
}

function changedFiles(root) {
  const output = run([
    'diff-tree', '--root', '--no-commit-id', '--numstat', '-r', 'HEAD'
  ], root);
  if (!output) return [];
  return output.split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).map((line) => {
    const parts = line.split('\t');
    if (parts.length < 3) return null;
    return { added: parts[0], deleted: parts[1], file: parts.slice(2).join('\t') };
  }).filter(Boolean);
}

module.exports = { run, repoRoot, hooksDir, lastCommit, changedFiles };
```

````text
/**
 * @returns {{system: string, user: string, events: object[], eventIds: Set<string>, inputTokens: number}}
 */
function build({ repo, openRecords = [], events = [], denyPaths = DEFAULT_DENY_PATHS }) {
  const kept = events.filter((e) => keepEvent(e, denyPaths)).map(cleanEvent);
  const payload = {
    repo: String(repo || '').slice(0, 120),

// Split events into batches, in seq order, so each request stays under the token cap.
function batchEvents(events, { maxInputTokens = 12000, openRecords = [], repo = '' } = {}) {

    estimateTokens(JSON.stringify({ repo, open_records: openRecords.slice(0, 60).map(cleanOpenRecord), events: [] }));

const DEFAULT_DENY_PATHS = ['.env', '.env.*', '*.pem', '*.key', 'id_rsa*', 'credentials*.json', 'secrets/**'];

function redact(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return { text: '', count: 0 };
  let count = 0;
  let redacted = text;
  for (const pattern of PATTERNS) {
    redacted = redacted.replace(pattern.regex, (...args) => {
      count++;

    if (c === '*' && glob[i + 1] === '*') { re += '.*'; i++; }

function redactPath(relPath, denyPaths = DEFAULT_DENY_PATHS) {

function str(value, max = MAX_STRING) {

  if (!text) return null;
  return text.slice(0, max);
}

function strList(value, max = MAX_LIST) {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return [];
  const out = [];
  for (const item of value) {
    const s = str(item);
    if (s && !out.includes(s)) out.push(s);
    if (out.length >= max) break;
  }
  return out;
}

// Rule 7: repo-relative, no "..", no drive letter, no leading slash.

    if (out.length >= MAX_LIST) break;

function parse(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return { ok: false, error: 'response was not text' };
  let body = text.trim();
  // Tolerate a fenced block even though the prompt forbids one.
  const fence = body.match(/^```(?:json)?\s*([\s\S]*?)\s*```$/);
  if (fence) body = fence[1].trim();
  if (!body) return { ok: false, error: 'empty response' };
  // Tolerate leading/trailing prose around a single JSON object.
  if (!body.startsWith('{')) {
    const start = body.indexOf('{');
    const end = body.lastIndexOf('}');
    if (start === -1 || end <= start) return { ok: false, error: 'no JSON object in response' };
    body = body.slice(start, end + 1);
  }
  try {
    const value = JSON.parse(body);
    if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {
````

````text
# memo

<!-- README to be dictated by Sunil -->
=====
# Security and privacy

What MEMO reads, what leaves your machine, and what you can delete.
Short version: MEMO is a local tool that writes Markdown and JSONL into your repo,
and sends batches of captured events to one API provider you configure.

## 1. What is captured

Capture only happens in a repo where you ran `memo init` (the repo is then listed in
`~/.memo/repos.json`). Claude Code calls `memo capture` on SessionStart, Stop, PreCompact
and SessionEnd; MEMO reads the new bytes of that session's transcript file.

Kept (`src/capture/claude.js`, limits from the plan §6.1):

| Event | What is stored | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `user_prompt` | your prompt text | 4,000 chars |
| `assistant_text` | the reply text | 3,000 chars |
| `tool_call` | tool name + the Bash command or the file path | 300 chars |
| `tool_result` | first 500 + last 300 chars, plus `ok: true/false` | 800 chars |
| `system`, `git_commit` | short marker lines | — |

Dropped before anything is written to disk:

- thinking blocks
- `Read` results (only the `tool_call` with the path is kept)
- `Write` / `Edit` content (path and line counts only)
- image blocks
- anything whose path matches `config.denyPaths`
  (default `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `credentials*.json`, `secrets/**`)

File paths are stored relative to the repo root. A path outside the repo becomes
`<outside-repo>`; your home directory is never written into the event text.

## 2. Redaction

`src/redact.js` runs twice: once when the event is written to disk, once again when the
prompt is built in `src/extract/prompt.js`. It removes API keys (`sk-ant-…`, `sk-proj-…`,
`AKIA…`, bearer tokens), credentials inside connection strings, `.env`-style
`NAME=value` lines and long high-entropy strings next to the words key/secret/token.

**Redaction is regex-based. It is a safety net, not a guarantee.** Read `.memory/` once
before you push a repo somewhere public. If a secret did land in a file, rotate the secret —
removing it from the current file does not remove it from older commits.

## 3. What is sent to the API

`memo process` (directly or from `memo cycle`) sends, per call:

- the fixed system prompt
- the repo folder name (not its full path)
- up to 60 open records (id, type, status, statement)
- one batch of event envelopes, capped at `maxInputTokensPerCall` (default 12,000 tokens)

Nothing else is uploaded: no file contents, no git remote, no username, no machine name.
Provider and model come from `~/.memo/config.json`. With `provider: "mock"` no network
call happens at all. With `apiEnabled: false` or `memo pause`, no call happens either.

Your provider's own retention and training policy applies to what you send — check it
and record the link in `docs/PHASE0_FINDINGS.md` §6 before using a real key.

## 4. Where data lives

| Location | Contents | In Git? |
|---|---|---|
| `.memory/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sid>.jsonl` | captured events | yes |
| `.memory/sessions/<sid>.md`, `index.json` | summaries, session index + tombstones | yes |
| `.memory/records/*.jsonl` | decisions, errors, tasks, learnings, facts, questions, intent | yes |
| `.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md`, `TASKS.md`, `progress.md` | generated reports | yes |
| `~/.memo/config.json`, `repos.json`, `state/`, `logs/` | machine state, cursors, jobs, usage | never |
| `~/.memo/personal.md` | your personal notes | never |

`memo commit` only ever stages `.memory/` (`git commit --only -- .memory`), never your
source files, and never pushes.

## 5. The API key

The key is read from the environment variable named by `config.apiKeyEnv`
(default `MEMO_API_KEY`, falling back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
It is never written into a config file, never logged, and only ever displayed as
`set (…last4)`.

`install_memo.bat` stores it with `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(…, 'User')`
after reading it with `Read-Host -AsSecureString`, so it is not echoed and not kept in
your shell history. It is still a plain user environment variable, readable by anything
running as you. DPAPI encryption is planned for P11.

## 6. Deleting data

```
memo clear --session <sid>                 # dry run: files, sizes, affected records
memo clear --session <sid> --with-derived --yes
memo clear --date 2026-10-21 --yes --confirm 2026-10-21
memo clear --record T-1b2c3d4e --yes
memo clear --all-repo-data --yes --confirm DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA
```

A deleted session gets a tombstone in `index.json`, so the next capture sweep does not
re-import it from the Claude transcript. The deletion itself is committed.

**Honest limit:** this removes the data from the current files only. Older Git commits
still contain it, and copies on GitHub or in other clones are unaffected. Full erasure
needs history rewriting (`git filter-repo` + force push), which MEMO does not do for you.

## 7. Turning it off

- `memo pause` — the scheduled task keeps running but does nothing
- `memo setup claude --remove` — removes the Claude Code hooks (a backup of
  `~/.claude/settings.json` is written first)
- `scripts\windows\uninstall_memo.bat` — removes the task, the logon entry and the hooks;
  it never deletes `.memory/` or `~/.memo` unless you type `DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA`

## 8. Trust boundaries

- The model's output is validated by `src/extract/validate.js` before anything is written:
  unknown fields are dropped, enums are enforced, `files` must be relative with no `..`.
  Model output is never executed, never used as a path outside `.memory/`, and never
  changes the config.
- `verified` / `done` are only accepted with a passing `tool_result` as evidence,
  otherwise they are downgraded and marked `downgraded: true`.
- Hooks and the scheduled task catch every error, log to `~/.memo/logs/` and exit 0,
  so a MEMO bug cannot fail your Claude Code session or your commit.
````

````text
# Phase 2 — API extraction

What `memo process` does: takes the events Phase 1 captured, sends only the **new** ones to
the configured model, validates the reply in code, and writes evidence-linked records plus a
session summary. Phase 1 behaviour is unchanged.

**Status: not executed.** The code below was written without running the test suite and
without any API call, on request. Nothing here is a claim that it works at runtime.

## New modules

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/config.js` | `~/.memo/config.json` load / sanitize / `set`; price table; API-key lookup (never prints the key) |
| `src/usage.js` | `chars/4` token estimate, cost per call, `~/.memo/logs/usage.jsonl`, monthly budget state |
| `src/store/records.js` | `.memory/records/*.jsonl` append-only op-log: ids, fold (last op wins), open records, job guard |
| `src/llm/provider.js` | interface, factory, `ProviderError{kind}`, 3 attempts with 2 s / 8 s / 30 s backoff, `retry-after`, 60 s abort |
| `src/llm/anthropic.js` | `POST /v1/messages` (`x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`) |
| `src/llm/openai.js` | `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `response_format: json_object` |
| `src/llm/mock.js` | replays `test/fixtures/llm/*.json`; simulates 429 / 500 / timeout / auth / quota / malformed |
| `src/extract/prompt.js` | fixed system rules, user payload, token-capped batching, **second redaction stage** |
| `src/extract/validate.js` | the §6.3 rules in code: enums, caps, evidence checks, downgrades |
| `src/extract/process.js` | jobs, idempotency, retries, budget, call cap, cursor advance |
| `src/report/session-summary.js` | `.memory/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sid>.md` |
| `scripts/try-extract.js` | one opt-in live call (`MEMO_LIVE=1`), not part of `npm test` |

## Commands

```
memo config                        print settings (key shown only as "set (…last4)")
memo config set <key> <value>      e.g. provider, model, monthlyBudgetUsd, apiEnabled,
                                   maxInputTokensPerCall, prices.<model>.inPerM
memo process                       process new events in every registered repo
memo process --dry-run             event count + estimated input tokens + estimated cost, no API call
memo process --repo <path>         one repo only
memo process --retry-failed        retry jobs parked as failed_permanent / failed_retryable
```

## What stops a surprise bill

- No new events → no call at all (`no_new_data`).
- `--dry-run` never constructs a provider and never calls one.
- `monthlyBudgetUsd` (default $5) is checked before every call, from real provider token counts.
- `maxInputTokensPerCall` (default 12,000) caps one request; `maxCallsPerCycle` (default 6) caps a run, and the leftover backlog is reported.
- `memo config set apiEnabled false` (or `paused true`) stops processing while capture keeps running.

## Privacy

Redaction runs twice: once at capture (Phase 1, on disk) and again in `extract/prompt.js`
before anything leaves the machine. Events are sent with `id, seq, ts, type, tool, text, ok,
truncated` only — no transcript line numbers, no uuids, no absolute paths. Any event whose
text names a denylisted path (`.env`, `*.pem`, `secrets/**`, …) is dropped from the request.
The key is read from the env var named by `apiKeyEnv` (fallback `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` /
`OPENAI_API_KEY`), is never written to a log, and provider logs carry only status, kind,
attempt and request id.

## How the model is kept honest

The model proposes; `extract/validate.js` decides. It drops unknown fields, enforces every
enum, caps strings at 500 chars and items at 25, drops any item whose evidence id is not in
the batch or an existing record, drops updates to ids that do not exist or whose type does not
match, requires `user_prompt` evidence for `intent`, and **downgrades** `verified` / `done` to
`resolved_unverified` / `implemented_unverified` with `downgraded: true` unless an evidence
event is a `tool_result` with `ok: true`. `auto_exec` is always written as `false`.

## Idempotency

Job id = `j-` + 10 hex of `sha1(sid:from:to)`, and every record line carries its `job`. If a
run crashes after records were appended but before `processedThrough` advanced, the next run
sees the job in the record files, advances the cursor and makes no call. `processedThrough` in
`.memory/sessions/index.json` is always written last.

## How to test this by hand (nothing below has been run)

```bash
npm test                       # the offline suite: no key, no network
memo process --dry-run         # event count, token estimate, cost estimate, zero calls
```

Offline, with the mock provider (no key needed):

```bash
memo config set provider mock
MEMO_MOCK_LLM=decision memo process
cat .memory/records/decisions.jsonl
cat .memory/sessions/2026/10/21/<sid>.md
memo process                   # expect "no_new_data" and no new usage line
```

Then the real thing, once `docs/PHASE0_FINDINGS.md` §7 names a model:

```bash
memo config set provider anthropic
memo config set model claude-haiku-5-5     # confirm this is the model you picked
setx MEMO_API_KEY "<key>"                  # new terminal afterwards
memo process --dry-run                     # check the estimate first
memo process
```

Worth checking by eye on the first real run:

1. every `evidence` id in `.memory/records/*.jsonl` exists in that session's `.jsonl`;
2. nothing is marked `verified` / `done` that no passing tool result supports;
3. the session `.md` summary matches what actually happened;
4. a second `memo process` adds no records and no line to `~/.memo/logs/usage.jsonl`;
5. with the network off: an error is logged, nothing is deleted, and the next run picks up where it stopped.

One live call against a fixture, costing one request:

```bash
MEMO_LIVE=1 node scripts/try-extract.js error-then-fix
```

## Open points

- **Model id is a default, not a decision.** `docs/PHASE0_FINDINGS.md` §7 is still a template,

- Reports (`PROJECT_STATE.md`, `TASKS.md`), `memo commit`, the 15-minute worker and
  `memo clear` are Phase 3–5 and are not part of this change.
````

```text
**Rate limit response headers** (the docs say the other headers are always included, but `retry-after` is only set on a 429):

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `retry-after` | Seconds to wait before retrying. |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` | Request cap, which refers to requests per day (RPD). |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` | Token cap, which refers to tokens per minute (TPM). |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` | Requests left under the RPD limit. |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` | Tokens left under the TPM limit. |
| `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` | Time until the RPD limit resets. |
| `x-ratelimit-reset-tokens` | Time until the TPM limit resets. |

**429 behaviour:** When you exceed a limit, the API returns "`429 Too Many Requests`". `retry-after` is set only in that case, and it gives the wait time in seconds.
```

 `https://console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs`

````text
**Response formats:** Structured Outputs uses `response_format` with `type: "json_schema"`, where `json_schema` contains a `name`, an optional `strict` flag, and a `schema`. The page also describes JSON Object Mode, set with `type: "json_object"`, which guarantees valid JSON syntax but not schema compliance.

**Models supporting `json_schema`:**
- **Strict mode (`strict: true`):** `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, `meta-models/muse-spark-open`
- **Best-effort mode (`strict: false`):** the same four models, plus `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`
- Other models can use JSON Object Mode only.

**Request shape:**

```json
{
  "response_format": {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
      "name": "schema_name",
      "strict": true,
      "schema": { ... }
    }
  }
}
```

Strict mode requires all properties to be listed in `required`, and every object must set `additionalProperties: false`. Optional fields can be modeled as nullable union types, such as `["string", "null"]`. Streaming and tool use are not supported with Structured Outputs.

**Validation failures:** In best-effort mode, a response that doesn't match the schema can return an HTTP 400 with the message "Generated JSON does not match the expected schema. Please adjust your prompt." The page does not specify an error code or a `failed_generation` field. Strict mode is designed to avoid these errors.
````

```text
**Reasoning controls for `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `openai/gpt-oss-120b`:**

- **`reasoning_effort`**: Accepts `low`, `medium`, or `high`. Higher values use more reasoning tokens.
- **`include_reasoning`**: `true` returns reasoning in `message.reasoning` and is the default. `false` excludes it.
- **`reasoning_format`**: Not supported for these models. The page states that "the `reasoning_format` parameter is not supported."
- `include_reasoning` and `reasoning_format` are mutually exclusive.

**Compatibility with `response_format` (`json_object`/`json_schema`):** The page does not say whether GPT-OSS models support these. It mentions `json_object` only in the parameter table, and it does not mention `json_schema`. Its JSON-mode note about `reasoning_format` does not apply to these models, since they don't support that parameter.

**Do reasoning tokens count toward `max_completion_tokens`?** The page does not say. It describes `max_completion_tokens` as the "Maximum length of model's response" and notes that the default "may be too low for complex reasoning," but it doesn't state whether reasoning tokens are included in that limit.
```

````text
The page doesn't mention `json_validate_failed` or `failed_generation`. Its only 400 entry is the generic description below, so for those specific codes you'd need another source, such as the Structured Outputs docs or Groq support.

**Error body shape**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "String - description of the specific error",
    "type": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

The `error` object contains `message` (a description meant to help you diagnose the problem) and `type` (a category such as `"invalid_request_error"`).

**Codes you asked about**

- **400 Bad Request:** "The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax." Review the request format.
- **413 Request Entity Too Large:** "The request body is too large." Reduce the size of the request body.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** "Too many requests were sent in a given timeframe." Add request throttling and respect rate limits.
- **498 Custom: Flex Tier Capacity Exceeded:** Groq's custom code for when the flex tier is at capacity and the request won't be processed. Try again later.
- **503 Service Unavailable:** The server isn't ready to handle the request, often due to maintenance or overload. Wait before retrying. Requests that return server error codes are not billed.
````

```text
/**
 * @param {string|object} response  raw provider text, or an already-parsed object
 * @param {object} ctx { eventIds: Set<string>, events: object[], existing: Map<id, record> }
 * @returns {{ok, error?, summary, items, dropped, notes, gaps}}
 */
function validate(response, ctx = {}) {
  const eventIds = ctx.eventIds instanceof Set ? ctx.eventIds : new Set(ctx.eventIds || []);
  const events = new Map((ctx.events || []).map((e) => [e.id, e]));
  const existing = ctx.existing instanceof Map ? ctx.existing : new Map();

  let body = response;
  if (typeof response === 'string') {
    const parsed = parse(response);
    if (!parsed.ok) return { ok: false, error: parsed.error, summary: '', items: [], dropped: [], notes: [], gaps: [] };
    body = parsed.value;
  }
  if (!body || typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body)) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'top level JSON must be an object', summary: '', items: [], dropped: [], notes: [], gaps: [] };
  }

  const dropped = [];
  const notes = [];
  const items = [];
  const summary = str(body.session_summary, MAX_SUMMARY) || '';
  const gaps = strList(body.gaps, 10);
  const rawItems = Array.isArray(body.items) ? body.items.slice(0, MAX_ITEMS) : [];
  if (Array.isArray(body.items) && body.items.length > MAX_ITEMS) {
    notes.push('items truncated to ' + MAX_ITEMS);
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < rawItems.length; i++) {
    const raw = rawItems[i];
    const drop = (reason) => dropped.push({ index: i, reason });
    if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) { drop('not an object'); continue; }

    const op = raw.op === 'update' ? 'update' : raw.op === 'create' ? 'create' : null;
    if (!op) { drop('op must be create or update'); continue; } // delete only comes from `memo clear`

    // Rule 3: evidence must point at this batch or at a known record.
    const evidence = [];
    for (const id of strList(raw.evidence, MAX_LIST)) {
      if (eventIds.has(id) || existing.has(id)) evidence.push(id);
    }
    if (evidence.length === 0) { drop('no usable evidence id'); continue; }

    let type;
    let id = null;
    if (op === 'update') {
      id = str(raw.id, 64);
      if (!id) { drop('update without id'); continue; }
      const prev = existing.get(id);
      if (!prev) { drop('update id does not exist: ' + id); continue; } // rule 4
      const claimed = str(raw.type, 40);
      if (claimed && claimed !== prev.type) { drop('update type mismatch for ' + id); continue; }
      type = prev.type;
    } else {
      type = str(raw.type, 40);
      if (!records.typeInfo(type)) { drop('unknown type: ' + raw.type); continue; }
    }
    const info = records.typeInfo(type);
    if (!info) { drop('unknown type: ' + type); continue; }

    const item = { op, type, evidence };
    if (id) item.id = id;

    // Status: enforce the enum; a create may fall back to the type default.
    let status = str(raw.status, 40);
    if (status && !info.statuses.includes(status)) {
      if (op === 'update') { drop('invalid status for ' + type + ': ' + status); continue; }
      notes.push('status "' + status + '" invalid for ' + type + ' → ' + info.default);
      status = null;
    }
    if (!status) {
      if (op === 'update') { drop('update without a usable status'); continue; }
      status = info.default;
    }

    // Rule 5: verified/done need a passing tool_result in this item's evidence.
    const proven = evidence.some((eid) => {
      const event = events.get(eid);
      return event && event.type === 'tool_result' && event.ok === true;
    });
    const fallback = DOWNGRADE[type] && DOWNGRADE[type][status];
    if (fallback && !proven) {
      status = fallback;
      item.downgraded = true;
    }
    item.status = status;

    // Rule 6: intent needs user_prompt evidence.
    if (type === 'intent') {
      const fromPrompt = evidence.some((eid) => {
        const event = events.get(eid);
        return event && event.type === 'user_prompt';
      });
      if (!fromPrompt) { drop('intent without user_prompt evidence'); continue; }
    }

    const statement = str(raw.statement) || (type === 'task' ? str(raw.title) : null);
    if (op === 'create' && !statement) { drop('create without statement'); continue; }
    if (statement) item.statement = statement;

    const rationale = str(raw.rationale);
    if (rationale) item.rationale = rationale;
    const confidence = str(raw.confidence, 20);
    if (confidence && records.CONFIDENCES.includes(confidence)) item.confidence = confidence;
    const files = cleanFiles(raw.files);
    if (files.length > 0) item.files = files;
    const supersedes = str(raw.supersedes, 64);
    if (supersedes && existing.has(supersedes)) item.supersedes = supersedes;
    for (const key of ['related', 'conflict_with']) {
      const list = strList(raw[key], MAX_LIST).filter((rid) => existing.has(rid));
      if (list.length > 0) item[key] = list;
    }

    if (type === 'task') {
      const title = str(raw.title, 200) || statement;
      if (title) item.title = title;
      const priority = str(raw.priority, 20);
      item.priority = priority && records.PRIORITIES.includes(priority) ? priority : 'unranked';
      const effort = str(raw.effort_estimate, 40);
      if (effort) {
        item.effort_estimate = effort;
        item.effort_basis = 'estimated';
      }
      const capability = str(raw.capability, 20);
      if (capability && records.CAPABILITIES.includes(capability)) item.capability = capability;
      const reason = str(raw.capability_reason);
      if (reason) item.capability_reason = reason;
      const blockers = strList(raw.blockers, 10);
      if (blockers.length > 0) item.blockers = blockers;
      const completion = strList(raw.completion_evidence, 10).filter((eid) => eventIds.has(eid) || existing.has(eid));
      if (completion.length > 0) item.completion_evidence = completion;
      // The model never gets to arm task execution.
      item.auto_exec = false;
    }

    items.push(item);
  }

  return { ok: true, summary, items, dropped, notes, gaps };
}

module.exports = { validate, parse, MAX_ITEMS, MAX_STRING, MAX_SUMMARY, DOWNGRADE, cleanFile };

// One live extraction call against a captured-transcript fixture. Opt-in only:
//   MEMO_LIVE=1 node scripts/try-extract.js error-then-fix
// Costs money. Not part of `npm test`, never called by the worker.

const fs = require('node:fs');
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');

const config = require('../src/config');
const { normalize } = require('../src/capture/claude');
const prompt = require('../src/extract/prompt');
const { validate } = require('../src/extract/validate');
const providerFactory = require('../src/llm/provider');
const { MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS } = require('../src/extract/process');
const usage = require('../src/usage');

function fixturePath(name) {
  if (fs.existsSync(name)) return name;
  const file = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'test', 'fixtures', 'claude', name.endsWith('.jsonl') ? name : name + '.jsonl');
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error('fixture not found: ' + name);
  return file;
}

function eventsFrom(file) {
  const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
  const ctx = { sid: 'live-try', root, cwd: root, home: os.homedir(), tools: {}, denyPaths: config.load().denyPaths };
  const out = [];
  let seq = 0;
  let lineNo = 0;
  for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
    lineNo++;
    if (!line.trim()) continue;
    let obj;
    try { obj = JSON.parse(line); } catch (_) { continue; }
    ctx.lineNo = lineNo;
    ctx.raw = line;
    for (const env of normalize(obj, ctx)) out.push({ ...env, seq: ++seq });
  }
  return out;
}

async function main() {
  const name = process.argv[2];
  if (!name) {
    process.stderr.write('usage: MEMO_LIVE=1 node scripts/try-extract.js <fixture>\n');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  if (process.env.MEMO_LIVE !== '1') {
    process.stderr.write('refusing to call the API: set MEMO_LIVE=1 to allow one live call\n');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const cfg = config.load();
  if (!config.apiKey(cfg)) {
    process.stderr.write('no API key in env ' + config.keyEnvName(cfg) + '\n');
    process.exit(1);
  }
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// API keys, stored once per machine and never inside a repo.
//
// Lookup order: the env var named by config.apiKeyEnv → the provider's usual env var
// (GROQ_API_KEY, …) → the stored credential in ~/.memo/secrets/<provider>.*
//
// Windows: the key is encrypted with DPAPI for the current Windows user
// (ConvertFrom-SecureString), so the file is useless on another account or machine.
// Elsewhere: a 0600 plain file. MEMO_SECRET_BACKEND=file forces the plain file (tests).
// The key travels to and from PowerShell over stdin/stdout only, never on a command line.

const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');
const { spawnSync } = require('node:child_process');
const { memoHome } = require('./paths');

const NAME_RE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$/;
const ENCRYPT_PS = '$k=[Console]::In.ReadToEnd().Trim(); if(-not $k){exit 3}; ' +
  '[Console]::Out.Write((ConvertTo-SecureString $k -AsPlainText -Force | ConvertFrom-SecureString))';
const DECRYPT_PS = '$e=[Console]::In.ReadToEnd().Trim(); $s=ConvertTo-SecureString $e; ' +
  '$b=[Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($s); ' +
  'try{[Console]::Out.Write([Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($b))}' +
  'finally{[Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($b)}';

const cache = new Map();

function backend() {
  if (process.env.MEMO_SECRET_BACKEND === 'file') return 'file';
  return process.platform === 'win32' ? 'dpapi' : 'file';
}

function secretsDir() {
  return path.join(memoHome(), 'secrets');
}

function safeName(name) {
  const n = String(name || '').toLowerCase();
  if (!NAME_RE.test(n)) throw new Error('invalid credential name: ' + name);
  return n;
}

function fileFor(name, kind = backend()) {
  return path.join(secretsDir(), safeName(name) + (kind === 'dpapi' ? '.dpapi' : '.key'));
}

function powershell(script, input) {
  const res = spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-Command', script], {
    input, encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true, timeout: 30000
  });
  if (res.error) throw new Error('PowerShell is not available: ' + res.error.message);
  if (res.status !== 0) throw new Error('PowerShell DPAPI call failed (exit ' + res.status + ')');
  return String(res.stdout || '').trim();
}

function validKey(key) {
  const k = String(key || '').trim();
  if (k.length < 8 || k.length > 512 || /\s/.test(k)) return null;
  return k;
}

function store(name, key) {
  const k = validKey(key);
  if (!k) throw new Error('that does not look like an API key (8–512 characters, no spaces)');
  const kind = backend();
  const file = fileFor(name, kind);
  fs.mkdirSync(secretsDir(), { recursive: true });
  const body = kind === 'dpapi' ? powershell(ENCRYPT_PS, k) : k;
  if (!body) throw new Error('encryption returned nothing');
  const tmp = file + '.' + process.pid + '.tmp';
  fs.writeFileSync(tmp, body + '\n', { encoding: 'utf8', mode: 0o600 });
  fs.renameSync(tmp, file);
  try { fs.chmodSync(file, 0o600); } catch (_) { /* not supported on every fs */ }
  cache.set(safeName(name), k);
  return { file, backend: kind };
}

function has(name) {
  try { return fs.existsSync(fileFor(name)); } catch (_) { return false; }
}

// Decrypted key, or '' when none is stored or it cannot be read.
function read(name) {
  const n = safeName(name);
  if (cache.has(n)) return cache.get(n);
  const kind = backend();
  let raw;
  try { raw = fs.readFileSync(fileFor(n, kind), 'utf8').trim(); } catch (_) { return ''; }
  if (!raw) return '';
  let key = '';
  try { key = kind === 'dpapi' ? powershell(DECRYPT_PS, raw) : raw; } catch (_) { key = ''; }
  key = validKey(key) || '';
  cache.set(n, key);
  return key;
}

function remove(name) {
  cache.delete(safeName(name));
  let removed = false;
  for (const kind of ['dpapi', 'file']) {
    try { fs.unlinkSync(fileFor(name, kind)); removed = true; } catch (_) { /* absent */ }
  }
  return removed;
}

function clearCache() {
  cache.clear();
}

module.exports = { backend, secretsDir, fileFor, store, has, read, remove, validKey, clearCache };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// What the provider says about its own limits, and when MEMO must not call it.
//
//   ~/.memo/state/limits.json    last rate-limit headers seen per provider/model
//   ~/.memo/state/cooldown.json  {until, reason, kind} — no API call before `until`
//
// Nothing here assumes a quota. Limits are only what the provider reported, with a timestamp.
// Groq documents x-ratelimit-limit-requests (per day), x-ratelimit-limit-tokens (per minute),
// the matching -remaining-/-reset- headers, and retry-after on 429
// (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits, read 22 Oct 2026). OpenAI uses the same names.

const path = require('node:path');
const { memoHome } = require('../paths');
const { readJson, writeJsonAtomic, isoLocal } = require('../util');

// Waiting longer than this inside one run is not worth it: defer to a later cycle instead.
const MAX_INLINE_WAIT_MS = 65000;
// No reset time given (credits exhausted, auth): look again after this long.
const DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS = { quota: 60 * 60000, auth: 60 * 60000, rate_limited: 15 * 60000 };

function limitsPath() {
  return path.join(memoHome(), 'state', 'limits.json');
}

function cooldownPath() {
  return path.join(memoHome(), 'state', 'cooldown.json');
}

function safeRead(file, fallback) {
  try { return readJson(file, fallback) || fallback; } catch (_) { return fallback; }
}

// "7.66s", "2m59.56s", "1h2m3s", "120ms", "30" (seconds) → ms, or null.
function parseDuration(raw) {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined) return null;
  const text = String(raw).trim();
  if (!text) return null;
  if (/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(text)) return Math.round(Number(text) * 1000);
  const re = /(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(ms|h|m|s)/g;
  let total = 0;
  let matched = false;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {
    matched = true;
    const n = Number(m[1]);
    total += m[2] === 'h' ? n * 3600000 : m[2] === 'm' ? n * 60000 : m[2] === 's' ? n * 1000 : n;
  }
  return matched ? Math.round(total) : null;
}

function num(v) {
  const n = Number(v);
  return v !== null && v !== undefined && v !== '' && Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null;
}

// Rate-limit headers → plain object (only fields the provider actually sent).
function fromHeaders(headers) {
  if (!headers || typeof headers.get !== 'function') return null;
  const get = (name) => headers.get(name);
  const out = {
    limitRequests: num(get('x-ratelimit-limit-requests')),
    remainingRequests: num(get('x-ratelimit-remaining-requests')),
    resetRequestsMs: parseDuration(get('x-ratelimit-reset-requests')),
    limitTokens: num(get('x-ratelimit-limit-tokens')),
    remainingTokens: num(get('x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens')),
    resetTokensMs: parseDuration(get('x-ratelimit-reset-tokens'))
  };
  for (const k of Object.keys(out)) if (out[k] === null) delete out[k];
  return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : null;
}

// "Please try again in 7m12.5s" in an error message → ms.
function retryHintMs(message) {
  const m = String(message || '').match(/try again in\s+([0-9hms.]+)/i);
  return m ? parseDuration(m[1]) : null;
}

// "Limit 8000, Requested 9512" in a too-large / TPM message → 8000.
function limitFromMessage(message) {
  const m = String(message || '').match(/\bLimit\s+(\d+)/i);
  return m ? Number(m[1]) : null;
}

function key(provider, model) {
  return String(provider) + '/' + String(model);
}

function record(provider, model, info) {
  if (!info) return null;
  const all = safeRead(limitsPath(), {});
  const entry = { ...(all[key(provider, model)] || {}), ...info, ts: isoLocal() };
  all[key(provider, model)] = entry;
  try { writeJsonAtomic(limitsPath(), all); } catch (_) { /* advisory */ }
  return entry;
}

function get(provider, model) {
  return safeRead(limitsPath(), {})[key(provider, model)] || null;
}

function cooldown(now = Date.now()) {
  const c = safeRead(cooldownPath(), null);
  if (!c || !c.until) return null;
  const until = Date.parse(c.until);
  if (!Number.isFinite(until) || until <= now) return null;
  return { ...c, ms: until - now };
}

function setCooldown(kind, ms, reason) {
  const wait = Number.isFinite(ms) && ms > 0 ? ms : DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS[kind] || DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS.rate_limited;
  const value = { kind, until: isoLocal(Date.now() + wait), reason: String(reason || kind).slice(0, 300), set: isoLocal() };
  try { writeJsonAtomic(cooldownPath(), value); } catch (_) { /* advisory */ }
  return value;
}

function clearCooldown() {
  try { require('node:fs').unlinkSync(cooldownPath()); return true; } catch (_) { return false; }
}

/**
 * Largest input budget for one call: the configured cap, lowered so that input + output
 * fits a tokens-per-minute limit the provider reported (headers or a 413 message).
 */
function inputCap(cfg, provider = cfg.provider, model = cfg.model) {
  const configured = Number(cfg.maxInputTokensPerCall);
  const seen = get(provider, model);
  const tpm = seen && (seen.learnedTokenLimit || seen.limitTokens);
  if (!tpm) return configured;
  const room = Math.floor(tpm * 0.85) - Number(cfg.maxOutputTokens || 0);
  return Math.max(1000, Math.min(configured, room));
}

/**
 * Before one call: go, wait a little, or defer to a later cycle.
 * @returns {{go: true} | {waitMs: number} | {deferMs: number, reason: string}}
 */
function gate(provider, model, needTokens, now = Date.now()) {
  const seen = get(provider, model);
  if (!seen || !seen.ts) return { go: true };
  const age = now - Date.parse(seen.ts);
  if (!Number.isFinite(age)) return { go: true };
  if (seen.remainingRequests === 0 && Number.isFinite(seen.resetRequestsMs) && age < seen.resetRequestsMs) {
    return { deferMs: seen.resetRequestsMs - age, reason: 'provider request limit reached (reported ' + seen.limitRequests + ')' };
  }
  if (Number.isFinite(seen.remainingTokens) && seen.remainingTokens < needTokens &&
      Number.isFinite(seen.resetTokensMs) && age < seen.resetTokensMs) {
    const wait = seen.resetTokensMs - age + 250;
    return wait <= MAX_INLINE_WAIT_MS ? { waitMs: wait }
      : { deferMs: wait, reason: 'provider token limit reached (reported ' + seen.limitTokens + ')' };
  }
  return { go: true };
}

module.exports = {
  MAX_INLINE_WAIT_MS, DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS, limitsPath, cooldownPath,
  parseDuration, fromHeaders, retryHintMs, limitFromMessage, record, get,
  cooldown, setCooldown, clearCooldown, inputCap, gate
};
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// JSON Schema of the extraction reply, for providers with strict structured output
// (Groq gpt-oss: console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs, read 22 Oct 2026).
// Strict mode needs every property in `required` and additionalProperties:false, so
// optional fields are nullable. extract/validate.js still checks everything afterwards.

const nullable = (type) => ({ type: [type, 'null'] });

const ITEM = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  properties: {
    op: { type: 'string', enum: ['create', 'update'] },
    id: nullable('string'),
    type: nullable('string'),
    statement: nullable('string'),
    title: nullable('string'),
    status: nullable('string'),
    confidence: nullable('string'),
    evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    files: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    rationale: nullable('string'),
    priority: nullable('string'),
    effort_estimate: nullable('string'),
    capability: nullable('string'),
    capability_reason: nullable('string')
  }
};
ITEM.required = Object.keys(ITEM.properties);

const EXTRACTION = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  properties: {
    schema: { type: 'integer' },
    session_summary: { type: 'string' },
    items: { type: 'array', items: ITEM },
    gaps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }
  },
  required: ['schema', 'session_summary', 'items', 'gaps']
};

module.exports = { EXTRACTION, NAME: 'memo_extraction' };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// OpenAI-compatible chat completions over raw fetch (zero dependencies). Serves two providers:
//
//   groq    POST https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions   (V1 default)
//   openai  POST <baseUrl or https://api.openai.com/v1>/chat/completions
//
// headers  Authorization: Bearer <key>, content-type: application/json
// body     {model, max_completion_tokens, response_format?, messages, reasoning_effort?, include_reasoning?}
// reply    {id, model, choices:[{message:{content}}], usage:{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}}
//
// Groq shape checked against console.groq.com/docs (models, structured-outputs, reasoning,
// rate-limits), 22 Oct 2026, and by live calls recorded in docs/V1_REQUIREMENTS.md.
// response_format: strict json_schema on models Groq lists for strict mode, else json_object.
// If a host rejects json_schema, the call is repeated once with json_object.
// OpenAI itself: json_object; the Responses API is not used.

const { ProviderError, postJson, withRetries, errorFor } = require('./provider');
const limits = require('./limits');
const { apiKey } = require('../config');

const URL = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions';
const GROQ_URL = 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions';
// console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs: strict json_schema support (22 Oct 2026).
const GROQ_STRICT = new Set(['openai/gpt-oss-20b', 'openai/gpt-oss-120b', 'qwen/qwen3.8-27b', 'meta-models/muse-spark-open']);

// config.baseUrl points the same wire format at any OpenAI-compatible host
// (Gemini's /v1beta/openai, OpenRouter, a local Ollama, …).
function endpoint(cfg) {
  if (cfg && cfg.baseUrl) return cfg.baseUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/chat/completions';
  return cfg && cfg.provider === 'groq' ? GROQ_URL : URL;
}

// 'json_schema' | 'json_object' | 'none' for one call.
function formatFor(cfg, model, { json = true, schema = null } = {}) {
  if (!json) return 'none';
  const wanted = cfg.responseFormat || 'auto';
  if (wanted === 'none') return 'none';
  if (wanted === 'json_schema') return schema ? 'json_schema' : 'json_object';
  if (wanted === 'json_object') return 'json_object';
  if (cfg.provider === 'groq' && !cfg.baseUrl && schema && GROQ_STRICT.has(model)) return 'json_schema';
  return 'json_object';
}

function responseFormat(format, schema) {
  if (format === 'json_schema') {
    return { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: schema.name, strict: true, schema: schema.schema } };
  }
  if (format === 'json_object') return { type: 'json_object' };
  return undefined;
}

function textOf(body) {
  const choice = body && Array.isArray(body.choices) ? body.choices[0] : null;
  const message = choice && choice.message;
  if (!message) return '';
  if (typeof message.content === 'string') return message.content.trim();
  if (Array.isArray(message.content)) {
    return message.content
      .filter((part) => part && typeof part.text === 'string')
      .map((part) => part.text)
      .join('')
      .trim();
  }
  return '';
}

function errorMessage(name, status, text) {
  let detail = '';
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(text);
    if (parsed && parsed.error && typeof parsed.error.message === 'string') detail = parsed.error.message;
  } catch (_) { /* non-JSON error body */ }
  return name + ' ' + status + (detail ? ': ' + detail.slice(0, 200) : '');
}

function create(cfg, opts = {}) {
  const name = cfg.provider === 'groq' ? 'groq' : 'openai';
  const key = opts.apiKey !== undefined ? opts.apiKey : apiKey(cfg);
  // Once a host refuses json_schema, stay on json_object for the rest of this run.
  let schemaRefused = false;

  async function once({ system, user, maxTokens, model, format, schema }) {
    const body = {
      model,
      max_completion_tokens: maxTokens,
      messages: [{ role: 'system', content: system }, { role: 'user', content: user }]
    };
    const rf = responseFormat(format, schema);
    if (rf) body.response_format = rf;
    if (name === 'groq' && /^openai\/gpt-oss/.test(model)) {
      if (cfg.reasoningEffort) body.reasoning_effort = cfg.reasoningEffort;
      body.include_reasoning = false;
    }
    const res = await postJson(endpoint(cfg), {
      headers: { authorization: 'Bearer ' + key },
      body,
      timeoutMs: opts.timeoutMs,
      fetchImpl: opts.fetchImpl
    });
    const requestId = (res.headers && typeof res.headers.get === 'function' && res.headers.get('x-request-id')) || null;
    const seen = limits.fromHeaders(res.headers);
    if (seen) limits.record(name, model, seen);
    if (res.status !== 200) {
      const err = errorFor(name, res, errorMessage(name, res.status, res.text), requestId);
      if (err.kind === 'too_large' && err.limit) limits.record(name, model, { learnedTokenLimit: err.limit });
      throw err;
    }
    let parsed;
    try { parsed = JSON.parse(res.text); } catch (err) {
      throw new ProviderError(name + ' returned invalid JSON envelope', { kind: 'retryable', status: res.status, requestId });
    }
    const usage = parsed.usage || {};
    return {
      text: textOf(parsed),
      usage: { input: Number(usage.prompt_tokens) || 0, output: Number(usage.completion_tokens) || 0 },
      model: parsed.model || model,
      requestId: parsed.id || requestId,
      format,
      limits: seen
    };
  }

  return {
    name,
    model: cfg.model,
    async complete({ system, user, maxTokens = 2000, model = cfg.model, json = true, schema = null }) {
      if (!key) throw new ProviderError('no API key for ' + name + ' — run `memo key set`', { kind: 'auth' });
      let format = formatFor(cfg, model, { json, schema });
      if (format === 'json_schema' && schemaRefused) format = 'json_object';
      return withRetries(name, async () => {
        try {
          return await once({ system, user, maxTokens, model, format, schema });
        } catch (err) {
          if (format === 'json_schema' && err.kind === 'bad_request' && /response_format|json_schema|schema/i.test(err.message)) {
            schemaRefused = true;
            format = 'json_object';
            return once({ system, user, maxTokens, model, format, schema });
          }
          throw err;
        }
      }, opts);
    }
  };
}

module.exports = { create, URL, GROQ_URL, GROQ_STRICT, endpoint, formatFor, textOf };
```

```javascript
'use strict';

// Token/cost accounting: ~/.memo/logs/usage.jsonl + budget checks (§6.4, §10.4).
// Tokens are what the provider reported; cost is always an estimate from config.prices.
// Mock calls are logged with mock:true and never counted as real usage.

const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');
const { logsDir } = require('./paths');
const { log } = require('./log');
const { priceFor } = require('./config');
const { isoLocal } = require('./util');

// Plan §6.3: estimate tokens as chars / 4.
function estimateTokens(text) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') return 0;
  return Math.ceil(text.length / 4);
}

// USD for one call, or null when the model has no price in config.
function costOf(cfg, model, inTokens, outTokens) {
  const price = priceFor(cfg, model);
  if (!price) return null;
  const cost = (Number(inTokens) || 0) / 1e6 * price.inPerM + (Number(outTokens) || 0) / 1e6 * price.outPerM;
  return Math.round(cost * 1e6) / 1e6;
}

function usageFile() {
  return path.join(logsDir(), 'usage.jsonl');
}

// One line per successful provider call: {ts, repoId, job, provider, model, in, out, costEst, mock?}.
function record(entry) {
  log('usage', {
    repoId: entry.repoId || null,
    job: entry.job || null,
    provider: entry.provider || null,
    ...(entry.mock ? { mock: true } : {}),
    model: entry.model || null,
    in: Number(entry.in) || 0,
    out: Number(entry.out) || 0,
    costEst: entry.costEst === null || entry.costEst === undefined ? null : Number(entry.costEst)
  });
}

function readLog(name) {
  const out = [];
  // log.js rotates to <file>.1 at 1 MB; read it too so a month total is not cut short.
  const file = path.join(logsDir(), name + '.jsonl');
  for (const f of [file + '.1', file]) {
    let raw;
    try { raw = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'); } catch (_) { continue; }
    for (const line of raw.split('\n')) {
      if (!line.trim()) continue;
      try { out.push(JSON.parse(line)); } catch (_) { /* torn line ignored */ }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function isMock(line) {
  return line.mock === true || line.provider === 'mock' || line.model === 'mock';
}

function currentMonth() {
  return isoLocal().slice(0, 7);
}

function today() {
  return isoLocal().slice(0, 10);
}

// Real calls whose local timestamp starts with prefix (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD).
// costKnown is false if any call had no price.
function totals(prefix) {
  const out = { period: prefix, calls: 0, input: 0, output: 0, costUsd: 0, costKnown: true, mockCalls: 0, lastTs: null };
  for (const line of readLog('usage')) {
    if (typeof line.ts !== 'string' || !line.ts.startsWith(prefix)) continue;
    if (line.model === undefined && line.in === undefined) continue;
    if (isMock(line)) { out.mockCalls++; continue; }
    out.calls++;
    out.lastTs = line.ts;
    out.input += Number(line.in) || 0;
    out.output += Number(line.out) || 0;
    if (line.costEst === null || line.costEst === undefined) out.costKnown = false;
    else out.costUsd += Number(line.costEst) || 0;
  }
  out.costUsd = Math.round(out.costUsd * 1e6) / 1e6;
  return out;
}

function monthTotals(month = currentMonth()) {
  const t = totals(month);
  return { month, ...t };
}

function dayTotals(day = today()) {
  return totals(day);
}

// Plan §P2 step 1: stop before a call when this month's estimated cost, or today's
// provider-reported tokens, already reached the configured budget.
function budgetState(cfg, month = currentMonth()) {
  const t = monthTotals(month);
  const limit = Number(cfg.monthlyBudgetUsd);
  const monthly = Number.isFinite(limit) && limit >= 0 && t.costUsd >= limit;
  const daily = Number(cfg.dailyTokenBudget) || 0;
  const day = daily > 0 ? dayTotals() : null;
  const dailyReached = Boolean(day && day.input + day.output >= daily);
  let reason = null;
  if (monthly) reason = 'monthly budget of ' + limit + ' USD reached (estimated cost)';
  else if (dailyReached) reason = 'daily token budget of ' + daily + ' reached';
  return { reached: monthly || dailyReached, reason, limit, dailyTokenBudget: daily, dayTokens: day ? day.input + day.output : null, ...t };
}

// Failed provider attempts in provider.jsonl whose timestamp starts with prefix, by kind.
function failures(prefix = currentMonth()) {
  const out = { total: 0, byKind: {}, last: null };
  for (const line of readLog('provider')) {
    if (typeof line.ts !== 'string' || !line.ts.startsWith(prefix) || line.provider === 'mock') continue;
    const kind = line.kind || 'unknown';
    out.total++;
    out.byKind[kind] = (out.byKind[kind] || 0) + 1;
    out.last = line;
  }
  return out;
}

module.exports = {
  estimateTokens, costOf, record, usageFile, readLog, totals, monthTotals, dayTotals, failures,
  budgetState, currentMonth, today
};
```

```text
'use strict';

// Provider HTTP behaviour with an injected fetch. No network, no key, no waiting.

const test = require('node:test');
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const fs = require('node:fs');
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');

const provider = require('../src/llm/provider');
const anthropic = require('../src/llm/anthropic');
const openai = require('../src/llm/openai');
const config = require('../src/config');

const KEY = 'sk-ant-test-0000000000000000000000000000';

function cfg(extra) {
  return { ...config.defaults(), ...extra };
}

// Minimal Response stand-in: only what the providers read.
function reply(status, body, headers = {}) {
  const map = new Map(Object.entries(headers).map(([k, v]) => [k.toLowerCase(), String(v)]));
  return {
    status,
    headers: { get: (name) => (map.has(String(name).toLowerCase()) ? map.get(String(name).toLowerCase()) : null) },
    text: async () => (typeof body === 'string' ? body : JSON.stringify(body))
  };
}
```
